sections.title: Agent learns each field without a soil test
sections.label: REAL DATA
sections.question: Can the agent learn how fast a field dries and how much water it holds, from its own probes?
sections.how: Real measured soil water from USDA SCAN stations. For each rain-free spell, each method predicts how much the root zone dries; the prediction is compared with what the probes measured. The agent learns only from earlier spells. Spells: 337.

sections.meaning: Learning lowers the error against the FAO 56 textbook values by 4.28 mm per spell (95% interval 2.69–6.04), at 6 of 6 stations.

sections.title: How long can an irrigation wait?
sections.label: IN-MODEL
sections.question: If the farmer cannot irrigate today (no power, no labour), how many days can he wait without losing yield?
sections.how: Every one of 421 irrigation advices on the unseen seasons was delayed 1 to 6 days and the season re-scored. 'Safe' = costs at most 0.05 points of yield.
sections.meaning: Early in the season most irrigations can wait about a week; from flowering on, about half cannot wait 3 days. The advice tells the farmer this.
sections.limit: Crop model; weather known in hindsight.

sections.title: What does asking the farmer first cost?
sections.label: IN-MODEL
sections.question: The pump only runs after approval. If the farmer is often unavailable, how much yield is lost?
sections.how: Same unseen seasons; on each day an advised irrigation happens only if the farmer is available. 'Plans for it' = the agent expects the wait to the next available day.
sections.meaning: Asking first costs well under a quarter of a point on average; planning for the wait halves the worst case. The calendar suffers most.
sections.limit: Crop model; availability patterns are assumed (PSPCL rota from 2011).

sections.title: When is the fertiliser reminder needed?
sections.label: IN-MODEL
sections.question: PAU ties the 2nd urea dose to the 2nd irrigation (about day 50–55). Sensor scheduling moves that irrigation. How often?
sections.how: Counted on the same unseen seasons with the FAO 56 rule.
sections.meaning: In most seasons the PAU 55-day fallback applies, so the agent reminds the farmer (it quotes PAU; it never computes a dose).
sections.limit: Crop model; reminder wording to be confirmed with the guide.

sections.title: Battery: why the probes are switched off between readings
sections.label: ESTIMATE
sections.question: How long does the node last on one 5,600 mAh battery?
sections.how: Datasheet currents (80 mA awake 2 s, 120 mA radio 0.25 s, 10 µA sleep, 5 mA per probe, 15 mAh/day regulator: assumed) × wakes per day from the season run.
sections.meaning: Switching the probes off is what matters (two weeks vs most of a season). The bench measures the real currents to replace these assumptions.
sections.limit: Estimate until measured with the INA219 on the bench.
